title: Tunisian knit stitch — the knit V from a crochet hook
subtitle: Insert through the stitch from front to back to make a knit-looking V face
excerpt: Tunisian knit stitch (TKS) inserts the hook through the body of each stitch from front to back — rather than under the vertical bar — on the forward pass. The change in insertion angle produces a knit V on the fabric face. TKS is the Tunisian stitch that most closely resembles stockinette knitting.

glossaryTerms.definition: Abbreviated TKS. Forward pass: insert hook from front to back through the centre of each stitch — between the front and back vertical bars — and draw up a loop. Return pass is the same as all Tunisian stitches: yarn over, pull through 1, then *yarn over, pull through 2 to end.

content.text: is the most knit-like of the Tunisian stitches. The hook enters through the centre of each stitch's body — from front to back between the two vertical bars — rather than under the surface bar. This angle twists the new loop around the stitch in the same way a knit stitch crosses its yarn, and the result is a clean row of V-shapes on the fabric face.
Work a foundation row of Tunisian simple stitch (TSS) to establish the vertical bars.
Forward pass (TKS): insert the hook from front to back through the centre of the first stitch body — the hook tip passes between the front bar and the back bar of the stitch, emerging on the back.
Yarn over and draw up a loop. Continue across the row in this way — one loop per stitch.
Return pass: yarn over, pull through 1. *Yarn over, pull through 2. Repeat to end — same as all Tunisian return passes.

items.symptom: The fabric looks identical to TSS — the knit V is not forming
items.cause: Inserting under the front bar rather than through the stitch body
items.fix: The hook tip must push all the way through the stitch and emerge at the back before the draw-up. A shorter, firmer insertion just under the surface bar produces TSS, not TKS.

content.text: Alternating TKS and Tunisian purl stitch rows produces a Tunisian rib that closely resembles 1x1 knit rib. Tunisian full stitch is a more complex Tunisian variant that reduces the curl that TKS shares with TSS.
